title: "Summarize final clean data"
output: github_document
date: "2026-09-28"

# Objectives

* Read in the final clean metadata, sequences (fasta), and trees from the canonical 08_all-together directory
  - post-removal of temporal outliers, low-quality/identical sequences, dirty metadata
  - verify all tip names match seq_new
* Join corrected host taxonomy (duck/mallard fix) and multi-taxa groupings from 08_all-together/annot/
* Fill in subtypes and H5 clades from phylogenetically inferred assignments
* Make summary figures for cleaned aligned data

## Changes from v3

* Filled-in H5 (HA) clades + N types now read directly from the most recent subtype/clade fill-in
  run, `phylo/03_clusters/subtype_clades/2026-07-01_out/sample_filledin_N-type_HA-clade.csv`
  (identical to the `08_all-together/annot/` copy used in v3 as of 2026-09-28; checked: 41366
  samples, no clade/N-type differences). Join now asserts no duplicate samples, every sample
  matched, and no blank clades
* New H5 clade plot set (mirrors the subtype-through-time plots): proportion barplots by year,
  stacked N-sample barplots by year, and smoothed proportional stacked density (sums to 1), each
  for the full date range and 1996+. New hierarchical clade palette (`clade.cols`), saved to
  `h5_clade_colors.csv`
* Smoothed proportional density plots added for subtype too, for consistency across plot sets
* Composites renumbered Fig 1 -> Fig 2 and Fig S1 -> Fig S2 (manuscript numbering); only the
  `_map` versions are output. New 5-panel layout: A year-count / B subtype / C H5 clade stacked
  and touching (year axis on C only), D host, E map; larger year-axis text, bold legend titles,
  bigger subtype (+20%) / clade (+10%) legend text, larger host colourbar. Map label fixes
  flagged as upstream TODO
* Bug fixes: duplicate-index column drop (`-which()` would drop ALL columns when none matched);
  country thresholds used `$N` (column is `n`) so the >=10/>=50 country plots were empty; host
  "<50" plot y-label said N<10

## Changes from v2

* Inputs switched from `phylo/.../rem_out/` to canonical `08_all-together/` (nuc_seq, phylo_trees, annot)
* Trees: FastTree `.tre` → IQTREE2 `.treefile`
* Host duck→mallard bug fixed via join with `sample_taxa_lookup_all` (see below)
* Subtype: phylogenetically filled subtypes (`sample_filledin_N-type_HA-clade.csv`) now used as primary via `coalesce(subtype_fill, subtype.raw)`; previously only patched mismatches and silently skipped NA subtypes
* Country rename: South Georgia entry was a bare unnamed string in `str_replace_all()` — silently ignored rather than substituted; now a proper named vector entry
* Name checks in read loop changed from silent `all()` evaluation to `stopifnot()`
* Segment label now extracted from filename rather than assumed from sort-index position

## Ins and outs
```{r}
# Canonical clean data from 08_all-together
f.in.nuc   <- "../08_all-together/nuc_seq/"
f.in.tree  <- "../08_all-together/phylo_trees/"
f.in.annot <- "../08_all-together/annot/"
# most recent phylogenetic fill-in of N types (NA tree) and H5 clades (HA tree)
f.in.fill  <- "../../phylo/03_clusters/subtype_clades/2026-07-01_out/sample_filledin_N-type_HA-clade.csv"

meta.in  <- list.files(path = f.in.nuc,  pattern = "_meta\\.csv$",   full.names = T) %>% mixedsort()
fasta.in <- list.files(path = f.in.nuc,  pattern = "\\.fasta$",      full.names = T) %>% mixedsort()
tree.in  <- list.files(path = f.in.tree, pattern = "\\.treefile$",   full.names = T) %>% mixedsort()
stopifnot(length(meta.in) == length(fasta.in), length(fasta.in) == length(tree.in))
l.tre <- length(tree.in)

# outputs
today <- Sys.Date()
f.out <- paste0(today, "_out/")
if (!dir.exists(f.out)) {dir.create(f.out)}
```

# Read in final clean metadata, sequences, and trees
```{r}
segments <- c("PB2", "PB1", "PA", "HA", "NP", "NA", "M", "NS")

tree <- nuc <- meta <- replicate(n = l.tre, vector())
for (i in 1:l.tre) {
  nuc[[i]]  <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(fasta.in[i])
  meta[[i]] <- read.csv(meta.in[i])
  tree[[i]] <- read.tree(tree.in[i])

  # verify all names align (bug fix: was silently evaluated before)
  stopifnot(all(names(nuc[[i]]) %in% meta[[i]]$seq_new))
  stopifnot(all(tree[[i]]$tip.label %in% meta[[i]]$seq_new))

  # remove duplicate index cols (v3 used -which(), which drops ALL columns if none match)
  meta[[i]] <- meta[[i]] %>% select(-any_of(c("X", "X.1", "X.2")))

  # country name standardisation
  # v2 bug: the South Georgia entry was written as a single unnamed string inside c()
  # ("South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands = S. Georgia and Sandwich Is.")
  # str_replace_all ignores unnamed elements, so no substitution occurred.
  # Fixed: split into pattern = replacement as a proper named vector entry.
  meta[[i]]$country <- str_replace_all(meta[[i]]$country,
    c("USA"                                         = "United States",
      "Svalbard and Jan Mayen"                       = "Norway",
      "Czech Republic"                               = "Czechia",
      "Turkey"                                       = "Türkiye",
      "South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands" = "S. Georgia and Sandwich Is."))
}
```

## Fix host: replace duck->mallard errors via sample_taxa_lookup_all
```{r}
taxa.lookup <- read.csv(paste0(f.in.annot, "sample_taxa_lookup_all.csv"))

# join on sample; common is the corrected common name (fixed in 06_host/mallard_duck_fix.Rmd)
meta.all <- left_join(meta.all, taxa.lookup, by = "sample")

# replace the buggy host column with the corrected common name
meta.all$host.raw <- meta.all$host  # preserve original
meta.all$host     <- meta.all$common

# samples missing from taxa.lookup would get host=NA — catch this before proceeding
n.unmatched <- sum(is.na(meta.all$host) & !is.na(meta.all$host.raw))
if (n.unmatched > 0) warning(n.unmatched, " samples had no taxa.lookup match; host set to NA")
n.changed <- sum(meta.all$host.raw != meta.all$host, na.rm = T)
cat("Samples with host name corrected:", n.changed, "\n")

# a few hosts are recorded under a Latin/scientific name instead of a common name; swap them
# for the common name from latin_common_fix.txt. Block format: common name line, then Latin
# line, blank-separated. Matched case-insensitively so e.g. "Calidris tenuirostris" hits.
fix.raw      <- readLines("latin_common_fix.txt")
fix.raw      <- fix.raw[fix.raw != ""]
latin.common <- data.frame(common = fix.raw[c(T, F)],
                           latin  = fix.raw[c(F, T)],
                           stringsAsFactors = F)
mi <- match(tolower(meta.all$host), tolower(latin.common$latin))
meta.all$host[!is.na(mi)] <- latin.common$common[mi[!is.na(mi)]]
cat("Hosts renamed Latin->common:", sum(!is.na(mi)), "rows;",
    n_distinct(latin.common$latin[mi[!is.na(mi)]]), "distinct names\n")

# merge common-name synonyms / spelling variants that map to the same species onto the most-
# sampled name (host_common_merge.csv, from -> to; canonical chosen by dataset sample count).
# This collapses e.g. "Cougar" -> "Mountain lion". TODO: the canonical names should be adopted
# upstream in the 06_host taxonomy lookup in a future build (see readme) — done here locally so
# the summary plots/tables and reported unique-host counts are deduplicated now.
host.merge <- read.csv("host_common_merge.csv")
mm <- match(meta.all$host, host.merge$from)
meta.all$host[!is.na(mm)] <- host.merge$to[mm[!is.na(mm)]]
cat("Common-name synonyms merged:", sum(!is.na(mm)), "rows;",
    n_distinct(host.merge$from[mm[!is.na(mm)]]), "names\n")
```

## Fill in subtypes and H5 clades from phylogenetic nearest-neighbour algorithm
FLAG: the fill-in (phylo/03_clusters/subtype_clades/plot_fill_subtypes_v2.Rmd) only fills
MISSING N types (NA tree) and H5 clades (HA tree); existing labels are never changed. Tips whose
label disagrees with the clade they are nested in on the tree (e.g. an N3/N8 inside the N1 clade,
or an EA_nonGsGD-labelled tip nested inside 2.3.4.4b) were NOT corrected, and the flagging code in
that script is commented out/unrun. These mismatched labels are carried as-is into every subtype
and clade plot below, and blank tips next to them may have inherited a wrong label from their
nearest labelled neighbour.
```{r}
fill.sub <- read.csv(f.in.fill)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(fill.sub$sample))

# The fill file's `subtype` column still contains the original blank/"H5"-only values for
# samples that couldn't be typed from accession metadata alone. The authoritative filled
# value is N_type (e.g. "N1"), so reconstruct the full label as paste0("H5", N_type).
# Fall back to the raw subtype string only where N_type is genuinely missing.
fill.sub <- fill.sub %>%
  mutate(subtype_fill = if_else(!is.na(N_type), paste0("H5", N_type), subtype)) %>%
  select(sample, subtype_fill, clade_fill = clade, N_type)

meta.all <- left_join(meta.all, fill.sub, by = "sample")

# filled-in clade must be complete: every sample matched and no blank clade
stopifnot(all(meta.all$sample %in% fill.sub$sample))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(meta.all$clade_fill) | meta.all$clade_fill == ""))

meta.all$subtype.raw <- meta.all$subtype

# also recover subtypes that were blank in raw metadata but present in the genotype col
subtype.from.raw <- if_else(
  meta.all$subtype.raw == "" | is.na(meta.all$subtype.raw),
  meta.all$genotype,
  meta.all$subtype.raw)

# priority: paste0("H5", N_type) fill > genotype-col fallback > raw subtype string
meta.all$subtype <- coalesce(meta.all$subtype_fill, subtype.from.raw)

cat("Subtypes provided by fill file:", sum(!is.na(meta.all$subtype_fill)), "\n")
cat("Remaining blank after fill:    ", sum(meta.all$subtype == "" | is.na(meta.all$subtype)), "\n")
cat("Remaining H5-only after fill:  ", sum(meta.all$subtype == "H5", na.rm = T), "\n")
cat("Distinct filled H5 clades:     ", n_distinct(meta.all$clade_fill), "\n")
```

# Dataset date range and earliest/latest samples
```{r date-range}
# One row per sample: collection_date/subtype/location are sample-level (identical across the 8 segment rows).
# Order by dec.date (decimal date used for the temporal/phylo analysis): it is populated for every sample,
# including year-only collection_dates, so it gives a robust earliest/latest even at partial date precision.
samp <- meta.all %>%
  distinct(sample,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(sample,subtype,location,country,region,continent,collection_date,dec.date)

date.range <- samp %>%
  summarise(n_samples        = n(),
            earliest_year    = floor(min(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE)),
            latest_year      = floor(max(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE)),
            earliest_decdate = min(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE),
            latest_decdate   = max(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE))
print(date.range)

earliest.samp <- samp %>% filter(dec.date == min(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE))
latest.samp   <- samp %>% filter(dec.date == max(dec.date,na.rm = TRUE))

cat("\n--- Earliest sample(s) ---\n")
earliest.samp %>% select(sample,subtype,country,region,location,collection_date,dec.date) %>% print()
cat("\n--- Latest sample(s) ---\n")
latest.samp %>% select(sample,subtype,country,region,location,collection_date,dec.date) %>% print()

# save range and the extreme samples
write.csv(date.range,paste0(f.out,"dataset_date_range.csv"),row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bind_rows(earliest = earliest.samp,latest = latest.samp,.id = "extreme"),
          paste0(f.out,"earliest_latest_samples.csv"),row.names = FALSE)

#oceanie
oc<-samp %>% 
  filter(region=="Oceania")
table(oc$subtype, oc$collection_date)
oc[which(oc$collection_date=="2024-03-06"),]
#whyy is there a sequence of H5N1 from Australia in 2024.. EPI_ISL_19156871 lookup shows
# A/Victoria/149/2024 (EPI_ISL_19156871): human host, clade 2.3.2.1a, collected 2024-03-06.
# This is Australia's first human H5N1 case: a 2.5-year-old who became ill while visiting

# Virus is a reassortant: HA, NA, NP, NS closest to clade 2.3.2.1a from Bangladesh; other

# Influenza A(H5N1) virus clade 2.3.2.1a in traveler returning to Australia from India, 2024.
```

```{r}
segment.cols <- natparks.pals(name = "Yellowstone", n = length(segments))
segment.cols <- segment.cols[c(1, 5, 2, 4, 6, 3, 8, 7)]
names(segment.cols) <- segments

subtype.freq <- sub.count$subtype[order(sub.count$n, decreasing = T)]
# palette sized to subtype.freq, not unique(meta.all$subtype): the latter includes all 8 segment
# rows per sample and any residual NAs, causing more colours than names -> silent misassignment.
# Colours are still assigned in frequency order (same colours as v3)
subtype.cols <- natparks.pals(name = "Olympic", n = length(subtype.freq))
names(subtype.cols) <- subtype.freq
# factor / legend / stacking order: alphanumeric (H5N1, H5N2, ... H5N9)
subtype.ord <- mixedsort(subtype.freq)
```

## Setup H5 clade colors
```{r}
# Order clades alphanumerically by nomenclature hierarchy: 0, then the non-GsGD lineages
# (Am_nonGsGD, EA_nonGsGD), then 1, 1.1, ..., 2.3.4, 2.3.4.4, 2.3.4.4b, ..., 9. Pad each
# dot-separated level to 3 digits (keeping any letter suffix) so a string sort puts parents
# before children and 2.3.4.4 before 2.3.4.4b. This order is used for the factor levels
# (stacking), legends and colour shading in every clade plot.
clade.key <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(cl) {
    if (!grepl("^[0-9]", cl)) return(paste0("000_", cl))  # non-GsGD sort right after "0" (key "000")
    parts <- strsplit(cl, ".", fixed = T)[[1]]
    paste(sprintf("%03d%s", as.integer(str_extract(parts, "^[0-9]+")),
                  str_remove(parts, "^[0-9]+")), collapse = ".")
  }, USE.NAMES = F)
}
clade.ord <- sort(unique(meta.all$clade_fill))
clade.ord <- clade.ord[order(clade.key(clade.ord))]

# 54 clades is too many for one interpolated qualitative palette (neighbours become a gradient),
# so colour hierarchically: each major lineage gets a distinct base hue (NatParks colours) and its
# sub-clades are light->dark shades of it, in clade.ord order. Base hues are restricted to reds,
# blues, purples and greys (no greens/yellows) so clade colours don't overlap with the subtype
# palette (Olympic greens/yellows).
# TODO (future): coordinate the subtype and clade palettes so co-occurring labels share a similar
# shade (e.g. H5N1 and 2.3.4.4b). More involved: would need a subtype<->clade mapping.
clade.family <- function(cl) {
  case_when(grepl("nonGsGD", cl)        ~ "nonGsGD",
            grepl("^2\\.3\\.4\\.4", cl) ~ "2.3.4.4",
            grepl("^2\\.3\\.4", cl)     ~ "2.3.4",
            grepl("^2\\.3\\.2", cl)     ~ "2.3.2",
            grepl("^2\\.2", cl)         ~ "2.2",
            grepl("^2\\.1", cl)         ~ "2.1",
            grepl("^2", cl)             ~ "2 other",
            grepl("^[01]($|\\.)", cl)   ~ "0-1",
            TRUE                        ~ "3-9")
}
family.base <- c("0-1"     = "#213958",  # Triglav navy
                 "2.1"     = "#8087AA",  # Acadia periwinkle
                 "2.2"     = "#B47E83",  # DeathValley mauve
                 "2.3.2"   = "#8C2B0E",  # DeathValley rust
                 "2 other" = "#E9988C",  # Torres salmon
                 "2.3.4"   = "#386EC2",  # Triglav blue
                 "2.3.4.4" = "#E23B0E",  # Charmonix red
                 "3-9"     = "#7F4B89",  # Arches2 purple
                 "nonGsGD" = "#616571")  # Banff grey
shade.family <- function(base, k) {
  if (k == 1) return(base)
  ramp <- colorRampPalette(c("white", base, "black"))(101)
  ramp[round(seq(30, 72, length.out = k))]
}
clade.fam  <- clade.family(clade.ord)
clade.cols <- setNames(character(length(clade.ord)), clade.ord)
for (f in unique(clade.fam)) {
  clade.cols[clade.fam == f] <- shade.family(family.base[[f]], sum(clade.fam == f))
}
write.csv(data.frame(clade = clade.ord, family = clade.fam, color = unname(clade.cols)),
          paste0(f.out, "h5_clade_colors.csv"), row.names = F)

# shared legend bits for the clade plots (54 keys -> 18 rows x 3 columns, small keys)
clade.leg       <- guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 18, byrow = F))
clade.key.theme <- theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                         legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
                         legend.spacing.x = unit(0.1, "cm"))
```

## Plot N nucleotide sequences by segment, over time
```{r}
# NA segment name would read as NA (missing) — set to string
meta.all$segment[which(is.na(meta.all$segment))] <- "NA"
meta.all$segment <- factor(meta.all$segment, levels = segments)
meta.all.count   <- meta.all %>% dplyr::group_by(segment) %>% count()
meta.all.count$segment <- factor(meta.all.count$segment, levels = segments)

ggplot(meta.all) +
  geom_bar(aes(x = segment, fill = segment)) +
  geom_text(data = meta.all.count, aes(x = segment, label = paste0("n=", n), y = -4),
            vjust = 1.3, size = 2) +
  labs(y = "# clean nucleotide sequences", x = "Segment") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = segment.cols) +
  plot.theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "n.clean.seq.byseg.png"), height = 3, width = 4)

ggplot(meta.all) +
  geom_bar(aes(x = collection_year, fill = segment)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1960, 2025, by = 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(y = "# clean nucleotide sequences", x = "Collection year", fill = "Segment") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = segment.cols) +
  plot.theme.date

  filter(as.numeric(collection_year) >= 1996) %>%
```

## Facet by continent, bars by host
```{r}
meta.all$continent <- str_replace_all(meta.all$continent,
  c("South America" = "Americas", "North America" = "Americas"))

host.continent.count.yr <- meta.all %>%
  filter(segment == "HA") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(host, continent, collection_year) %>%
  count() %>% as.data.frame()
host.continent.count.yr$collection_year <- as.numeric(host.continent.count.yr$collection_year)
host.continent.count.yr$continent <- factor(host.continent.count.yr$continent,
  levels = c("Americas", "Asia", "Antarctica", "Europe", "Africa", "Oceania"))

host.continent.count.yr %>%
  filter(collection_year >= 1996) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = host, y = n, fill = collection_year), stat = "identity") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(y = "N H5Nx samples", x = NULL, fill = "Collection year") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1) +
  plot.theme.date +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.key.width = unit(2.5, "cm"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6)) +
  facet_wrap(~continent, scales = "free") +
  force_panelsizes(rows = c(1, 1), cols = c(2.4, 0.8, 0.1))
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "n.clean.samp.FacetWrap-continent.host.year.1996.png"),
```

## N samples by H5 clade
Same plot set as subtype through time, using the phylogenetically filled-in H5 (HA) clade
(`clade_fill`; complete, no NAs). Full date range and 1996+; no `*` date ticks.
```{r}
clade.count.yr <- meta.all %>%
  filter(segment == "HA") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(clade_fill, collection_year) %>%
  count() %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(collection_year) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(clade_fill = factor(clade_fill, levels = clade.ord),
         collection_year = as.numeric(collection_year))
write.csv(clade.count.yr, paste0(f.out, "n.clean.samp.byclade.year.csv"), row.names = F)

# every year in the data range, so years with no samples show as blank gaps (as for subtype)
yr.all <- as.character(seq(min(clade.count.yr$collection_year), max(clade.count.yr$collection_year)))

# proportion by year
p.prop.clade <- clade.count.yr %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = as.factor(collection_year), y = prop, fill = clade_fill),
           stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = yr.all,
                   breaks = as.character(seq(1960, 2025, by = 5)),
                   expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(y = "Proportion samples", x = "Collection year", fill = "H5 clade") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clade.cols) +
  plot.theme.date + clade.leg + clade.key.theme
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "prop.clean.samp.byclade.year.png"), plot = p.prop.clade, height = 3, width = 12)

p.prop.clade.1996 <- clade.count.yr %>%
  filter(collection_year >= 1996) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = as.factor(collection_year), y = prop, fill = clade_fill),
           stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = as.character(seq(2000, 2025, by = 5)), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(y = "Proportion samples", x = "Collection year", fill = "H5 clade") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clade.cols) +
  plot.theme.date + clade.leg + clade.key.theme
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "prop.clean.samp.byclade.year.1996.png"), plot = p.prop.clade.1996, height = 3, width = 6)

# N samples by year, stacked by clade
p.n.clade <- clade.count.yr %>%
```

# Summarize trimmed alignments
## Extract width, % ambiguous, % GC
```{r}
alpha.width <- replicate(n = l.tre, vector())

for (i in 1:l.tre) {
  alph     <- alphabetFrequency(nuc[[i]])
  rownames(alph) <- names(nuc[[i]])
  alph.df  <- alph %>% as.data.frame() %>% select(-c("-", "+", "."))
  total.width <- max(width(nuc[[i]]))

  df.out <- data.frame(
    tip.label   = rownames(alph),
    tot.width   = total.width,
    n.nuc       = NA, perc.cov    = NA,
    n.noambig   = NA, perc.noambig = NA,
    n.gc        = NA, perc.gc     = NA,
    perc.a = NA, perc.c = NA, perc.t = NA, perc.g = NA)

  for (j in 1:nrow(alph.df)) {
    df.out$n.nuc[j]   <- sum(alph.df[j,])
    df.out$perc.cov[j] <- round((df.out$n.nuc[j] / total.width) * 100, digits = 2)
    noambig              <- sum(alph.df[j, c("A", "T", "C", "G")])
    df.out$n.noambig[j]  <- noambig
    df.out$perc.noambig[j] <- round((noambig / total.width) * 100, digits = 2)
    df.out$n.gc[j]    <- sum(alph.df[j, c("C", "G")])
    df.out$perc.gc[j] <- round((df.out$n.gc[j] / noambig) * 100, digits = 2)
    df.out$perc.a[j]  <- round((alph.df$A[j] / noambig) * 100, digits = 2)
    df.out$perc.c[j]  <- round((alph.df$C[j] / noambig) * 100, digits = 2)
    df.out$perc.t[j]  <- round((alph.df$T[j] / noambig) * 100, digits = 2)
    df.out$perc.g[j]  <- round((alph.df$G[j] / noambig) * 100, digits = 2)
  }

  # extract segment name from filename instead of assuming index order (bug fix from v2)
  df.out$segment <- str_extract(basename(fasta.in[i]), paste(segments, collapse = "|"))
  alpha.width[[i]] <- df.out
}

alpha.width.all <- bind_rows(alpha.width)
alpha.width.all$segment <- factor(alpha.width.all$segment, levels = segments)

write.csv(alpha.width.all, paste0(f.out, "nuc.clean.align.summary.csv"))
```

# Composite cowplot
Figure numbering: the main summary composite is manuscript **Fig 2** and the full-date-range
version is **Fig S2** (v3 code/text called them Fig 1 / Fig S1). Only the `_map` composites are
output; the older region-barplot versions are commented out below.
```{r}
d_fix <- theme(axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
m     <- theme(plot.margin = margin(1, 2, 1, 2))  # tight top/bottom -> less space between rows
tag   <- theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))

# bold legend titles in the composites
leg.bold <- theme(legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5))  # +25% title size

# collection-year panels (A, B, C): larger axis text + titles
yr.txt <- theme(axis.text  = element_text(size = 10),
                axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))

# A, B, C are stacked with zero top/bottom margin. No "Collection year" axis title on any of
# them; the year labels (axis text) are shown only under A. B and C keep the 5-year tick marks.
m.stack  <- theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 0, 2))
m.A      <- theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 2, 6, 2))  # small gap between A and B
no.x.ttl <- theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
no.x.lab <- theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x  = element_blank())
no.leg   <- theme(legend.position = "none")
leg.of   <- function(p, pos = "bottom") cowplot::get_plot_component(p, paste0("guide-box-", pos))


# tags for the stacked panels sit in a left margin column (location "margin", position "left")
# so they don't add a strip above each panel and break the touching stack
tag.left <- theme(plot.tag.location = "margin", plot.tag.position = "left",
                  plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", vjust = 1))
# B and C: nudged down a little so the tag sits level with the legend title above the panel
tag.left.leg <- theme(plot.tag.location = "margin", plot.tag.position = "left",
                      plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", vjust = 1,
                                              margin = margin(t = 2)))
# tags for the wrapped right-hand panels (D host, E map): drawn in the top-left corner at a
# numeric position, which reserves no space (a normal "topleft" tag on E adds a strip to the
# top of its row, which also pushes C away from B)
tag.corner <- theme(plot.tag.position = c(0.005, 0.995),
                    plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0, vjust = 1))
# "E" tag: level with the map legend title and just left of it, matching the tag-to-title gap in
# B and C. The title starts ~11.5% across the trimmed map PNG (legend.margin left = 60 pt in
# map_global_geno.Rmd), so the tag's right edge sits at x = 0.092 (hjust = 1). Re-tune if the
# map legend margin changes.
tag.E <- theme(plot.tag.position = c(0.092, 1.008),
               plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 1, vjust = 1))

# subtype legend: ABOVE panel B, title above the keys (left-aligned), one row of tiles. Text and key size
# match the H5 clade legend; both legends start just right of the tag column (no negative
# margin, which made the "B" tag collide with the one-row legend title)
sub.leg   <- theme(legend.position = "top",
                   legend.justification = "left",
                   legend.location = "plot",
                   legend.margin = margin(2, 0, 2, 6),
                   legend.key.spacing.x = unit(2, "pt"),
                   legend.text = element_text(size = 9))
sub.guide <- guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0))
sub.key   <- theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.32, "cm"))

# H5 clade legend: ABOVE panel C, title above the keys (left-aligned, as subtype), 8 rows
# (54 clades -> 7 columns, filled down the columns). It must fit inside the left column or it
# runs under the map (E): at 9 pt text / 0.32 cm keys / 2 pt column spacing it is ~4.9 in wide
# (7 rows would be ~5.6 in, too wide), vs ~5.3 in left column (widths = c(1.6, 2) on 12 in)
clade.leg.comp <- list(
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 8, byrow = F, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0)),
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.justification = "left",
        legend.location = "plot",
        legend.margin = margin(2, 0, 2, 6),
        legend.key.spacing.x = unit(2, "pt"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.32, "cm")))

# host panel (D): larger collection-year colourbar, legend text/title and host (x axis) labels.
# Colourbar length is 5x key height, so keep key height modest or the bar overflows the panel
host.leg <- theme(legend.key.height = unit(0.42, "cm"),
                  legend.key.width  = unit(0.55, "cm"),
                  legend.text  = element_text(size = 9),   # same size as B / C legends
                  legend.title = element_text(size = 12.5, face = "bold"),  # same as B / C
                  axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 8, angle = 60, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))
# top room for the D tag; wide left margin opens the gap from panel A and moves D's y-axis title
# right, clear of the D tag
m.host   <- theme(plot.margin = margin(16, 2, 1, 24))
```

## Map panel for composite
Map panel (E) is a pre-rendered PNG from the map script in `05_annotate/05_compare_genotyping/`
(outputs now in `2026-09-28_map/`, previously `2026-07-01_map/`; same filenames). Label fixes
done upstream in the 2026-09-28 maps:

* DONE: larger, bold region-label font
* DONE: line breaks (`\n`) in multi-word labels so each centres over its region
* OPTIONAL / not done: semi-transparent white background behind labels (e.g.
  `geom_label(fill = alpha("white", 0.6), label.size = 0)` or `shadowtext`) if labels over dark
  fills still read poorly
```{r}
# Pre-rendered global choropleth of N samples per region (2020-2025), generated in
# 05_annotate/05_compare_genotyping/ (map_global_geno.Rmd). Read as a raster and wrap
# in ggdraw() so it behaves as a ggplot panel inside the patchwork composites below.
# This replaced the region barplot (p.region.1996 / p.region) in the *_map figures

# Flatten transparency onto white and trim the uniform white border. We intentionally do
# NOT crop the top band here — doing so clipped the compass rose / northern landmasses.
# The wrap_elements(full=) + scale (below) handle fit, so the full projection stays intact.
# In the composites p.map is wrapped in wrap_elements(full=) so it fills its whole grid
# cell (no axis alignment). Within that large cell, scale < 1 sizes the map so the entire
# projection + colorbar stay visible without spilling over the cell edges.
# Raise toward 1 to enlarge, lower to add margin.
map.png <- "../05_annotate/05_compare_genotyping/2026-09-28_map/map_n_samples_1996-2025_legend-top.png"

map.img <- magick::image_read(map.png)
map.img <- magick::image_flatten(magick::image_background(map.img, "white"))
map.img <- magick::image_trim(map.img, fuzz = 5)
# halign/valign pin the map to the top-left of its cell so its legend title (the top-most
# element of the trimmed image) sits at a known spot for the "E" tag (tag.E, below)
p.map   <- ggdraw() + draw_image(map.img, scale = 1.0, halign = 0, valign = 1)

# map for the full range of sample dates
map.full.png <- "../05_annotate/05_compare_genotyping/2026-09-28_map/map_n_samples_all-dates_legend-top.png"
map.img.full <- magick::image_read(map.full.png)
map.img.full <- magick::image_flatten(magick::image_background(map.img.full, "white"))
map.img.full <- magick::image_trim(map.img.full, fuzz = 5)
p.map.full   <- ggdraw() + draw_image(map.img.full, scale = 1.0, halign = 0, valign = 1)
```

## Fig 2 (map): main summary (1996+)
```{r}
# Layout (design grid, left column narrow):
#   A year-count (+ year labels)  | D host  (D wrapped: rows 1-2)
#   (subtype legend) B subtype density | D
#   B (cont.)                     | E map   (E wrapped: rows 3-4)
#   (clade legend) C H5 clade density  | E
# Panel heights A:B:C = 1:1.5:1.5 (B spans rows 2-3 = 1.05 + 0.45, giving D more height; legends/axes are added on top
# of these). Splitting B's row lets E (map) take more height than D. Year labels only under A;
# small gap under A (m.A). D and E are wrap_elements() so they don't align axes with the left
# column (D's tall host labels otherwise stretch the row's axis strip).
fig.design <- "AD\nBD\nBE\nCE"

# panel A: drop the per-bar count labels (geom_text) — too small to read at composite size.
# The standalone n.clean.samp.bycolldate.1996.png keeps them.
p.h5yr.1996.nolab <- p.h5yr.1996
p.h5yr.1996.nolab$layers <- Filter(function(l) !inherits(l$geom, "GeomText"), p.h5yr.1996.nolab$layers)

# B and C are the smoothed proportional density plots (dens.clean.samp.by*.year.1996). Their x is
# continuous and computed over the scale range, so give A, B, C the same limits (half a year past
# the first/last year, where A's bars end) -> year axes line up and the density fills the width
yr.max       <- max(as.numeric(meta.all$collection_year), na.rm = T)
yr.lim.1996  <- c(1995.5, yr.max + 0.5)
yr.scale.1996 <- scale_x_continuous(limits = yr.lim.1996, breaks = seq(2000, 2025, by = 5),
                                    expand = c(0, 0))

# density plots have no y padding, so where B/C touch the panel above their 1.00 / 0.00 labels
# collide with its bottom label; pad y a little (like the barplots' default expansion)
dens.y <- scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.04))

pB.1996 <- p.dens.sub.1996 + yr.scale.1996 + dens.y +
  yr.txt + sub.leg + sub.guide + sub.key + leg.bold
pC.1996 <- p.dens.clade.1996 + yr.scale.1996 + dens.y +
  yr.txt + clade.leg.comp + leg.bold

fig2.map <- (p.h5yr.1996.nolab + yr.scale.1996 + yr.txt + no.x.ttl + m.A + tag.left) +
            (pB.1996 + labs(y = "Proportion samples") + no.x.lab + m.stack + tag.left.leg) +
            (pC.1996 + labs(y = "Proportion samples") + no.x.lab + m.stack + tag.left.leg) +
            (wrap_elements(full = p.host100.1996 + d_fix + host.leg + m.host) + tag.corner) +
            (wrap_elements(full = p.map) + m + tag.E) +
  plot_layout(design = fig.design, widths = c(1.6, 2), heights = c(1, 1.05, 0.45, 1.5)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "Fig2_summary_1996_map.png"), plot = fig2.map,
       width = 12, height = 8.1, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Host taxonomy summary
How many unique common hosts are in the dataset, how many resolve to a complete species
via the 06_host multi-taxa taxonomic lookup, and how many unique species result.
```{r host-taxa-summary}
# unique common-name hosts in the cleaned dataset (host = corrected common name)
common.hosts <- sort(unique(meta.all$host[!is.na(meta.all$host)]))
cat("Unique common hosts in dataset:", length(common.hosts), "\n")

# taxonomic lookup from 06_host multi-taxa (common -> class/order/family/genus/species/eco_group)
host.taxa <- read.csv("../06_host/2026-01-27_out/complete_host_taxa_with_ecogroup_fixed.csv")
host.taxa <- host.taxa %>% distinct(common, .keep_all = TRUE)

host.match <- data.frame(common = common.hosts) %>%
  left_join(host.taxa[, c("common", "species")], by = "common") %>%
  mutate(has_species = !is.na(species) & species != "")

# backfill: hosts renamed by latin_common_fix.txt (e.g. Great knot) may not be keyed by their
# common name in the taxonomy lookup, but the Latin name we replaced IS the species binomial.
# For any such host still missing a species, fill it from that Latin name, using the canonical
# capitalized form from the lookup's species column where available. (latin.common is built in
# the host-fix chunk above.)
need <- !host.match$has_species & host.match$common %in% latin.common$common
if (any(need)) {
  lat   <- latin.common$latin[match(host.match$common[need], latin.common$common)]
  canon <- host.taxa$species[match(tolower(lat), tolower(host.taxa$species))]
  host.match$species[need]     <- ifelse(is.na(canon), lat, canon)
  host.match$has_species[need] <- TRUE
  cat("Species backfilled from Latin fix:", sum(need), "\n")
}

n.complete <- sum(host.match$has_species)
cat("Common hosts with a complete species:", n.complete, "of", length(common.hosts),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * n.complete / length(common.hosts)), "\n")
cat("Common hosts missing a species:      ", length(common.hosts) - n.complete, "\n")
cat("Unique species:", n_distinct(host.match$species[host.match$has_species]), "\n")

# common hosts that did not resolve to a species (for inspection / lookup gaps)
missing.hosts <- host.match$common[!host.match$has_species]
cat("\n--- Common hosts missing a species ---\n")
print(missing.hosts)

write.csv(host.match, paste0(f.out, "host_common_to_species.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
# readable plain-text version: one "common -> species" per line
writeLines(paste(host.match$common, host.match$species, sep = " -> "),
           paste0(f.out, "host_common_to_species.txt"))

# sorted list of the unique species present in the dataset (after the Latin->common host fix)
unique.species <- sort(unique(host.match$species[host.match$has_species]))
write.csv(data.frame(species = unique.species),
          paste0(f.out, "unique_species.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
# also a single comma-separated line, e.g. for pasting into text
cat(paste(unique.species, collapse = ", "), file = paste0(f.out, "unique_species.txt"))

# unique host common names (after the Latin->common fix), as CSV (one per row) and a single
# comma-separated text line
write.csv(data.frame(common = common.hosts),
          paste0(f.out, "unique_host_common.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(paste(common.hosts, collapse = ", "), file = paste0(f.out, "unique_host_common.txt"))

# unique species paired with the common name(s) they represent. csv: two columns
# (species, common); txt: a single line "common (Genus species), ...". common names are
# joined with "; " in the rare case a species still maps to more than one.
species.common <- host.match %>%
  filter(has_species) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(common = paste(sort(unique(common)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(common)
write.csv(species.common, paste0(f.out, "unique_species_common.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(paste0(species.common$common, " (", species.common$species, ")", collapse = ", "),
    file = paste0(f.out, "unique_species_common.txt"))
# RTF version: same list but the binomial is italicised ({\i ...}). RTF is plain text that
# Word / Pages / TextEdit open as formatted text (no extra R package needed).
sc.rtf <- paste0(species.common$common, " ({\\i ", species.common$species, "})", collapse = ", ")
writeLines(paste0("{\\rtf1\\ansi\\deff0 ", sc.rtf, "}"),
           paste0(f.out, "unique_species_common.rtf"))

# all common hosts paired with a taxon label: the Genus species where available, otherwise the
# lowest available rank (genus > family > order > class) from the 06_host taxonomy. Uses the
# backfilled species from host.match and falls through the higher ranks for the rest, so every
# host resolves to a label. csv: common, taxon, taxon_rank; txt: "common (taxon), ...".
host.taxon <- host.match %>%
  select(common, species) %>%
  left_join(host.taxa[, c("common", "genus", "family", "order", "class")], by = "common") %>%
  mutate(across(c(species, genus, family, order, class), ~ ifelse(.x == "", NA, .x)),
         taxon      = coalesce(species, genus, family, order, class),
         taxon_rank = case_when(!is.na(species) ~ "species", !is.na(genus) ~ "genus",
                                !is.na(family) ~ "family", !is.na(order) ~ "order",
                                !is.na(class) ~ "class", TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  select(common, taxon, taxon_rank) %>%
  arrange(common)
write.csv(host.taxon, paste0(f.out, "unique_host_common_taxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(paste0(host.taxon$common, " (", host.taxon$taxon, ")", collapse = ", "),
    file = paste0(f.out, "unique_host_common_taxon.txt"))
# RTF version: italicise the taxon only when it is a genus or species (family/order/class stay
# roman, per nomenclature convention).
ital      <- host.taxon$taxon_rank %in% c("species", "genus")
taxon.rtf <- ifelse(ital, paste0("{\\i ", host.taxon$taxon, "}"), host.taxon$taxon)
ht.rtf    <- paste0(host.taxon$common, " (", taxon.rtf, ")", collapse = ", ")
writeLines(paste0("{\\rtf1\\ansi\\deff0 ", ht.rtf, "}"),
           paste0(f.out, "unique_host_common_taxon.rtf"))
```

## Host taxonomy summary: H5 clade 2.3.4.4b only
Same counts as above, restricted to samples whose filled-in H5 clade (`clade_fill`, from
`sample_filledin_N-type_HA-clade.csv`) is 2.3.4.4b. Reuses `host.match` from the chunk above
(so the Latin-name backfill carries over). Run the host-taxa-summary chunk first.

NOTE (2026-09-28): four "host" entries are not animal hosts and should be dropped from the
reported unique-host counts: "Environment", "Cattle milk product", "Pet food", "Raw pet food".
None of them resolve to a species, so species counts are unaffected. Broad names (e.g. "Duck",
"Gull", "Seal") stay in the unique-host counts but not the species counts. Not yet applied in
code (counts printed by these chunks still include the four). Counts after the drop, from
2026-09-28_out/host_common_to_species*.csv:

* Entire dataset: 537 unique hosts (541 - 4), 442 unique species, 95 hosts without a species
* Clade 2.3.4.4b: 464 unique hosts (468 - 4), 384 unique species, 80 hosts without a species
```{r host-taxa-summary-2344b}
meta.b <- meta.all %>% filter(clade_fill == "2.3.4.4b")
cat("2.3.4.4b samples:", n_distinct(meta.b$sample), "\n")

common.hosts.b <- sort(unique(meta.b$host[!is.na(meta.b$host)]))
host.match.b   <- host.match %>% filter(common %in% common.hosts.b)

n.complete.b <- sum(host.match.b$has_species)
cat("2.3.4.4b unique common hosts:", length(common.hosts.b), "\n")
cat("2.3.4.4b common hosts with a complete species:", n.complete.b, "of", length(common.hosts.b),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * n.complete.b / length(common.hosts.b)), "\n")
cat("2.3.4.4b unique species:", n_distinct(host.match.b$species[host.match.b$has_species]), "\n")

write.csv(host.match.b, paste0(f.out, "host_common_to_species_2.3.4.4b.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
